title: Trump is losing the half-wars he has started
gist: Andrew Adonis argues that Trump’s serial confrontations—an all-out trade war on Canada, an 'economic D-Day' on Iran, and domestic assaults on migration, elections and universities—are consistently 'half-wars': maximalist rhetoric that stops short of delivery, destabilising the order without collapsing it, and often failing on its own terms.

insights.claim: Adonis argues Trump’s second-term hallmark is the 'half-war'—conflicts billed as maximalist that seriously destabilise the US and its relations without triggering a complete collapse of the established order.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: A lens for discounting Trump’s escalation threats when pricing geopolitical risk—rhetoric routinely exceeds delivery.
insights.locator: They are part of the pattern of half-wars

insights.claim: Adonis contends the worst forebodings of liberal internationalists—that Trump’s foreign policy leads to major global disorder—have not been realised after nearly two years of his second term.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: A calming counter to consensus alarm—useful for sizing actual versus perceived tail risk.
insights.locator: but the worst forebodings of liberal internationalists

insights.claim: Trump’s 50 per cent tariff escalation on Canada explicitly excluded crude oil and natural gas because the US depends heavily on those Canadian energy imports, leaving the highest-value imports unaffected.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: The energy carve-out means the tariff’s real trade impact is far narrower than headlines imply—key for commodity and cross-border flows.
insights.quote: strategically huge and vital energy sectors have been excluded, precisely because they are huge and vital
insights.locator: In reality, the highest-value US imports

insights.claim: The real target of the Canada trade war is the car industry, with Trump pressing manufacturers to relocate production from Canada to the US—a limited industrial-strategy fight, not a general economic rupture.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Narrows the exposure to autos rather than the whole $-trade relationship—relevant to auto-sector positioning.
insights.locator: Trump’s key target in this trade war

insights.claim: Adonis notes the pre-existing US–Mexico–Canada free trade agreement continues to apply to most trade between the countries despite the tariff escalation.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: The institutional trade backbone remains intact, limiting the disruption’s reach.
insights.locator: Beyond energy, the pre-existing free trade agreement

insights.claim: Adonis argues Trump’s Iran conflict is the one that is genuinely different in scale—a protracted military engagement that has destabilised world trade and radicalised the regime—yet has produced no ground invasion.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Distinguishes the one confrontation with real market and energy consequences from the rhetorical ones.
insights.locator: Trump’s conflict with Iran is on a wholly different plane

insights.claim: The Iran 'economic D-Day' is largely non-military, and its supposedly blanket sanctions on China, India and other traders with Iran do not take immediate effect and are not specific.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: The sanctions bark exceeds the bite—markets pricing in immediate blanket enforcement may be overreacting.
insights.quote: It is classic Trump that the “D-Day” he has just announced is nothing of the kind.

insights.claim: Adonis predicts November’s US midterm elections will be as free and fair as previous ones and that Trump is on course to lose them badly.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: A concrete political forecast that would shift the legislative balance and constrain Trump’s second half-term.
insights.locator: For all the foreboding to the contrary

insights.claim: The US Supreme Court, despite its partisan Republican majority, has curbed some Trump measures such as the assault on birthright citizenship rather than acting as a rubber stamp.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Institutional checks are holding better than feared—reduces the probability of unconstrained executive action.

insights.claim: Adonis notes Trump’s bullying of allies has had mixed results—Europe is paying more for US protection, but Zelensky has not surrendered to Putin’s demands.
insights.speaker: Andrew Adonis
insights.so_what: Track record of the coercion strategy—wins on burden-sharing, losses on Ukraine capitulation.
